------------------------------ MODULE W4Od13m0p3t2 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Slots, Instances

VARIABLES owner, ver, claimed, pslot, prver

vars == <<owner, ver, claimed, pslot, prver>>

NONE == "none"
IDLE == "idle"

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Instances \cup {NONE}]
    /\ ver \in [Slots -> 0..1]
    /\ claimed \in [Instances -> SUBSET Slots]
    /\ pslot \in [Instances -> Slots \cup {IDLE}]
    /\ prver \in [Instances -> 0..1]

Init ==
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ ver = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ claimed = [i \in Instances |-> {}]
    /\ pslot = [i \in Instances |-> IDLE]
    /\ prver = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

Read(i, s) ==
    /\ pslot[i] = IDLE
    /\ pslot' = [pslot EXCEPT ![i] = s]
    /\ prver' = [prver EXCEPT ![i] = ver[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, claimed>>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ pslot[i] # IDLE
    /\ LET s == pslot[i] IN
        /\ owner[s] = NONE
        /\ ver[s] = prver[i]
        /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = i]
        /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![s] = 1]
        /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![i] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ pslot' = [pslot EXCEPT ![i] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prver>>

RetryStale(i) ==
    /\ pslot[i] # IDLE
    /\ LET s == pslot[i] IN
        /\ owner[s] = NONE
        /\ ver[s] # prver[i]
    /\ pslot' = [pslot EXCEPT ![i] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, claimed, prver>>

GiveUp(i) ==
    /\ pslot[i] # IDLE
    /\ owner[pslot[i]] # NONE
    /\ pslot' = [pslot EXCEPT ![i] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ver, claimed, prver>>

Release(i, s) ==
    /\ owner[s] = i
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![i] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, pslot, prver>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Slots : Read(i, s)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Commit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : RetryStale(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : GiveUp(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Slots : Release(i, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A i, j \in Instances : i # j => (claimed[i] \cap claimed[j] = {})

=============================================================================
nl:
Vending machine network with a shared pool of dispensing slots. Two independent
controller instances, A and B, both serve the same physical pool of slots (they
share one pool). Each slot carries a version number and an owner field that is
initially unassigned. Because the two controllers act concurrently, each uses
optimistic locking with retry to claim a slot: a controller first reads a slot's
current version (a Read step), then later tries to commit the claim. A commit
only succeeds if the slot is still unowned AND its version equals the version the
controller originally read; on success the controller records the slot in its own
claimed set, sets the owner, and bumps the version. If the version has moved on
since the read (another controller committed in between), the commit fails and the
controller aborts its pending attempt so it can retry from a fresh read. A separate
give-up step lets a controller drop a pending attempt for a slot that has since been
taken by the other controller.

A controller may also Release a slot it owns (the item was dispensed / the slot was
restocked), returning the owner field to unassigned while leaving the version bumped,
so a later stale read is detected and retried.

Actions: Read (stage a versioned read of a slot), Commit (compare-and-swap claim on
success), RetryStale (abort a pending attempt whose read version is stale even though
the slot is currently free), GiveUp (abandon a pending attempt for an already-owned
slot), Release (drop ownership of an owned slot).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No slot is ever double-allocated across the two controllers -- the
set of slots claimed by controller A and the set claimed by controller B are always
disjoint.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od9m5p2t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Feeders, Voters

TOTAL == 3
MAXCAP == 3

VARIABLES load, pool, cap, votes, pend

vars == <<load, pool, cap, votes, pend>>

RECURSIVE SumF(_)
SumF(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
           ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN load[x] + SumF(S \ {x})

Quorum == (Cardinality(Voters) \div 2) + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in [Feeders -> 0..TOTAL]
    /\ pool \in 0..TOTAL
    /\ cap \in [Feeders -> 1..MAXCAP]
    /\ votes \in SUBSET Voters
    /\ pend \in [kind: {"none","shed","restore"}, f: Feeders]

Init ==
    /\ load = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ pool = TOTAL
    /\ cap = [f \in Feeders |-> MAXCAP]
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ pend = [kind |-> "none", f |-> CHOOSE f \in Feeders : TRUE]

Propose(k, f) ==
    /\ pend.kind = "none"
    /\ k \in {"shed","restore"}
    /\ (k = "shed") => load[f] >= 1
    /\ (k = "restore") => pool >= 1
    /\ pend' = [kind |-> k, f |-> f]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, pool, cap>>

Vote(v) ==
    /\ pend.kind # "none"
    /\ v \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, pool, cap, pend>>

CommitShed ==
    /\ pend.kind = "shed"
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
    /\ load[pend.f] >= 1
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![pend.f] = @ - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ pend' = [kind |-> "none", f |-> pend.f]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap>>

CommitRestore ==
    /\ pend.kind = "restore"
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
    /\ pool >= 1
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![pend.f] = @ + 1]
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ pend' = [kind |-> "none", f |-> pend.f]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap>>

Rerate(f, c) ==
    /\ c \in 1..MAXCAP
    /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![f] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, pool, votes, pend>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in {"shed","restore"}, f \in Feeders : Propose(k, f)
    \/ \E v \in Voters : Vote(v)
    \/ CommitShed
    \/ CommitRestore
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, c \in 1..MAXCAP : Rerate(f, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Conservation == pool + SumF(Feeders) = TOTAL

=============================================================================
nl:
A power-grid load shedder balances a fixed amount of electrical load across two
feeders and a spare pool. The grid was commissioned with a fixed total number of
load units; load is never created or destroyed, only moved between a feeder and the
spare pool when the shedder acts. Every move must be approved by a quorum of the
three regional controllers before it is applied (quorum voting on each action):
an operator first proposes a move (shed one unit from a feeder to the pool, or
restore one unit from the pool to a feeder), controllers cast approving votes, and
the move is applied only once a strict majority has voted, after which the pending
proposal is cleared. As a runtime twist, each feeder's rated capacity can be
re-rated up or down at any time; re-rating changes only the capacity ceiling, never
the amount of load actually present, so the conserved quantity is unaffected.

Actions: Propose (register a pending shed or restore of one unit), Vote (a controller
approves the pending proposal), CommitShed (apply an approved shed, pool gains the
unit the feeder loses), CommitRestore (apply an approved restore, feeder gains the
unit the pool loses), Rerate (change a feeder's capacity ceiling without moving load).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of load units, summed over both feeders and the
spare pool, is always exactly the fixed commissioned total -- load is neither created
nor destroyed by any shedding, restoring, or re-rating action.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od13m1p4t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Cells

N == Cardinality(Nodes)

VARIABLES holder, occupied, freecells, crashed

vars == <<holder, occupied, freecells, crashed>>

\* Nodes are integers 1..N so the ring successor is arithmetic.
Succ(n) == (n % N) + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Nodes
    /\ occupied \in SUBSET Cells
    /\ freecells \in SUBSET Cells
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Nodes

Init ==
    /\ holder = 1
    /\ occupied = {}
    /\ freecells = Cells
    /\ crashed = {}

\* The token holder, if alive, dispenses an item that consumes one free
\* capacity cell of the shared magazine.
Dispense(n, c) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ c \in freecells
    /\ occupied' = occupied \cup {c}
    /\ freecells' = freecells \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

PassToken(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ holder' = Succ(n)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, freecells, crashed>>

Crash(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) < N - 1
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, occupied, freecells>>

Reclaim ==
    /\ holder \in crashed
    /\ \E m \in Nodes : m \notin crashed
    /\ holder' = Succ(holder)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, freecells, crashed>>

Collect(c) ==
    /\ c \in occupied
    /\ occupied' = occupied \ {c}
    /\ freecells' = freecells \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, c \in Cells : Dispense(n, c)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : PassToken(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ Reclaim
    \/ \E c \in Cells : Collect(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every capacity cell of the shared magazine is accounted for exactly once:
\* occupied and free cells partition the fixed set of cells, so occupancy can
\* never exceed capacity.
CapacityCoherent ==
    /\ occupied \cup freecells = Cells
    /\ occupied \cap freecells = {}

=============================================================================
nl:
A network of vending machines is arranged in a token ring and shares one output
magazine. The magazine has a fixed set of capacity cells; each dispensed item that
is waiting to be collected occupies exactly one free capacity cell. Exclusive access
is enforced by a single circulating token: only the machine currently holding the
token is allowed to dispense, and dispensing consumes one currently-free capacity
cell (so a machine cannot dispense when the magazine is full). The token is passed
around the ring from one machine to the next. As a twist, any machine can crash
silently at any time; a crashed machine can no longer dispense or pass the token, so
the ring may reclaim the token from a crashed holder and hand it to the next live
machine. When a customer collects an item, its capacity cell is returned to the free
pool.

Actions: Dispense (the live token holder consumes one free capacity cell), PassToken
(the token holder hands the token to the next machine), Crash (a machine crashes
silently), Reclaim (the ring moves the token off a crashed holder to a live machine),
Collect (a customer frees the capacity cell of one occupied item).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The occupied capacity cells and the free capacity cells always
partition the magazine's fixed cell set exactly (no cell is both occupied and free,
and none is lost), so the number of items in the magazine can never exceed its
capacity.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Feeders

TOTAL == 3
MAXCAP == 3
NF == Cardinality(Feeders)

VARIABLES load, carried, holder, cap

vars == <<load, carried, holder, cap>>

Succ(f) == (f % NF) + 1

RECURSIVE SumL(_)
SumL(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
           ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN load[x] + SumL(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in [Feeders -> 0..TOTAL]
    /\ carried \in 0..TOTAL
    /\ holder \in Feeders
    /\ cap \in [Feeders -> 1..MAXCAP]

Init ==
    /\ load = [f \in Feeders |-> IF f = 1 THEN TOTAL ELSE 0]
    /\ carried = 0
    /\ holder = 1
    /\ cap = [f \in Feeders |-> MAXCAP]

Pickup ==
    /\ load[holder] >= 1
    /\ carried < TOTAL
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![holder] = @ - 1]
    /\ carried' = carried + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, cap>>

Drop ==
    /\ carried >= 1
    /\ load[holder] < TOTAL
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![holder] = @ + 1]
    /\ carried' = carried - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, cap>>

MoveToken ==
    /\ holder' = Succ(holder)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, carried, cap>>

Rerate(f, c) ==
    /\ c \in 1..MAXCAP
    /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![f] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, carried, holder>>

ForcedShed ==
    /\ load[holder] > cap[holder]
    /\ carried < TOTAL
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![holder] = @ - 1]
    /\ carried' = carried + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ Pickup
    \/ Drop
    \/ MoveToken
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, c \in 1..MAXCAP : Rerate(f, c)
    \/ ForcedShed

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Conservation == SumL(Feeders) + carried = TOTAL

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Feeders = {1, 2}
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A power-grid load shedder moves a fixed total number of load units around a ring of
feeders using a single maintenance token. The token holder is a mobile balancing car
that can carry load units between feeders. Only the feeder currently holding the
token may have load picked up from it or dropped onto it, and the token circulates
around the ring. Load is never created or destroyed: a unit picked up from a feeder
goes into the car's carried amount, and a unit dropped goes from the carried amount
back onto a feeder. As a runtime twist, each feeder's rated capacity can be re-rated
up or down at any time; if a re-rating leaves a feeder carrying more load than its new
ceiling, the token car may perform a forced shed of one over-limit unit into its
carried amount. Re-rating itself never moves any load.

Actions: Pickup (the token feeder loses one unit into the car's carried amount), Drop
(the car places one carried unit onto the token feeder), MoveToken (the token advances
to the next feeder in the ring, carrying any load with it), Rerate (change a feeder's
capacity ceiling without moving load), ForcedShed (move one over-ceiling unit off the
token feeder into the carried amount after a downward re-rating).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of load units, summed over all feeders plus the
amount currently carried by the token car, is always exactly the fixed total -- load
is neither created nor destroyed by picking up, dropping, moving, re-rating, or
forced shedding.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od18m9p4t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Doors, Keys

MAXEP == 2
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES assign, unlocked, epoch, pending, reqep

vars == <<assign, unlocked, epoch, pending, reqep>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ assign \in [Keys -> Doors \cup {NONE}]
    /\ unlocked \in SUBSET Doors
    /\ epoch \in 0..MAXEP
    /\ pending \in SUBSET Doors
    /\ reqep \in [Doors -> 0..MAXEP]

Init ==
    /\ assign = [k \in Keys |-> NONE]
    /\ unlocked = {}
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ reqep = [d \in Doors |-> 0]

Reconfig ==
    /\ epoch < MAXEP
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assign, unlocked, pending, reqep>>

RequestUnlock(d) ==
    /\ d \notin pending
    /\ d \notin unlocked
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {d}
    /\ reqep' = [reqep EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assign, unlocked, epoch>>

ApplyGrant(d, k) ==
    /\ d \in pending
    /\ reqep[d] = epoch
    /\ assign[k] = NONE
    /\ d \notin unlocked
    /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![k] = d]
    /\ unlocked' = unlocked \cup {d}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, reqep>>

DropStale(d) ==
    /\ d \in pending
    /\ reqep[d] < epoch
    /\ pending' = pending \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assign, unlocked, epoch, reqep>>

Revoke(d, k) ==
    /\ assign[k] = d
    /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![k] = NONE]
    /\ unlocked' = unlocked \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pending, reqep>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfig
    \/ \E d \in Doors : RequestUnlock(d)
    \/ \E d \in Doors, k \in Keys : ApplyGrant(d, k)
    \/ \E d \in Doors : DropStale(d)
    \/ \E d \in Doors, k \in Keys : Revoke(d, k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

KeyCoherent ==
    \A d \in Doors : (d \in unlocked) <=> (\E k \in Keys : assign[k] = d)

=============================================================================
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network unlocks doors by handing out a fixed set of unlock
keys; there are only as many keys as the security policy allows doors open at once,
so the keys are the capacity limit. The network is reconfigured from time to time,
and each reconfiguration bumps a global epoch number. A door is unlocked only when it
holds one of the keys. Because unlock requests travel over a mesh and can be reordered
or delayed, each door's pending unlock request is tagged with the epoch at which it was
issued; a request is honored only if its epoch still matches the current epoch, and a
request left stale by a reconfiguration is dropped rather than applied. Granting an
unlock consumes a free key and marks the door unlocked; revoking returns the key and
relocks the door.

Actions: Reconfig (bump the epoch, making outstanding requests potentially stale),
RequestUnlock (a door registers a pending unlock request tagged with the current
epoch), ApplyGrant (honor a fresh, non-stale request by assigning a free key and
unlocking the door), DropStale (discard a request whose epoch is older than the
current epoch), Revoke (return a key and relock the door).

SAFETY PROPERTY: A door is unlocked if and only if it currently holds one of the
finite set of unlock keys, so the number of simultaneously unlocked doors can never
exceed the key capacity.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od19m0p5t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Books, Patrons

AVAIL == "avail"
RES == "reserved"
ARCH == "archived"
NONE == "none"
IDLE == "idle"

VARIABLES status, resBy, archived, gen, pbook, pgen

vars == <<status, resBy, archived, gen, pbook, pgen>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ status \in [Books -> {AVAIL, RES, ARCH}]
    /\ resBy \in [Books -> Patrons \cup {NONE}]
    /\ archived \in SUBSET Books
    /\ gen \in [Books -> 0..1]
    /\ pbook \in [Patrons -> Books \cup {IDLE}]
    /\ pgen \in [Patrons -> 0..1]

Init ==
    /\ status = [b \in Books |-> AVAIL]
    /\ resBy = [b \in Books |-> NONE]
    /\ archived = {}
    /\ gen = [b \in Books |-> 0]
    /\ pbook = [p \in Patrons |-> IDLE]
    /\ pgen = [p \in Patrons |-> 0]

Flip(g) == 1 - g

ReadGen(p, b) ==
    /\ pbook[p] = IDLE
    /\ pbook' = [pbook EXCEPT ![p] = b]
    /\ pgen' = [pgen EXCEPT ![p] = gen[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, resBy, archived, gen>>

CommitReserve(p) ==
    /\ pbook[p] # IDLE
    /\ LET b == pbook[p] IN
        /\ status[b] = AVAIL
        /\ gen[b] = pgen[p]
        /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = RES]
        /\ resBy' = [resBy EXCEPT ![b] = p]
        /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![b] = Flip(@)]
    /\ pbook' = [pbook EXCEPT ![p] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<archived, pgen>>

RetryReserve(p) ==
    /\ pbook[p] # IDLE
    /\ LET b == pbook[p] IN ~(status[b] = AVAIL /\ gen[b] = pgen[p])
    /\ pbook' = [pbook EXCEPT ![p] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, resBy, archived, gen, pgen>>

Cancel(p, b) ==
    /\ status[b] = RES
    /\ resBy[b] = p
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = AVAIL]
    /\ resBy' = [resBy EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![b] = Flip(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<archived, pbook, pgen>>

Archive(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = AVAIL
    /\ b \notin archived
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = ARCH]
    /\ archived' = archived \cup {b}
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![b] = Flip(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<resBy, pbook, pgen>>

AdminArchive(b) ==
    /\ b \notin archived
    /\ status[b] # ARCH
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = ARCH]
    /\ resBy' = [resBy EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ archived' = archived \cup {b}
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![b] = Flip(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pbook, pgen>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : ReadGen(p, b)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : CommitReserve(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : RetryReserve(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons, b \in Books : Cancel(p, b)
    \/ \E b \in Books : Archive(b)
    \/ \E b \in Books : AdminArchive(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ArchiveCoherent ==
    \A b \in Books :
        /\ (status[b] = ARCH) <=> (b \in archived)
        /\ (status[b] = ARCH) => (resBy[b] = NONE)

=============================================================================
nl:
A library book reservation system lets patrons reserve books using optimistic locking
with retry, and lets books be permanently archived (withdrawn from circulation), which
is an irreversible action. Each book has a status (available, reserved, or archived)
and a generation tag that flips whenever the book is modified. To reserve a book, a
patron first reads the book's current generation, then tries to commit the reservation;
the commit succeeds only if the book is still available and its generation still
matches the value read, otherwise the attempt is abandoned and retried. A reservation
can be cancelled, returning the book to available. Archiving is the irreversible step:
an available book may be archived at most once, moving it permanently to the archived
status and recording it in the archive ledger. A privileged admin override can archive
a book even if it is currently reserved, clearing any reservation in the process, but
still only once per book.

Actions: ReadGen (a patron stages an optimistic read of a book's generation),
CommitReserve (finalize a reservation when the book is still available and unchanged),
RetryReserve (abandon a reservation attempt that can no longer commit, for retry),
Cancel (release a reservation back to available), Archive (irreversibly archive an
available book, recording it once in the ledger), AdminArchive (privileged override
that archives any not-yet-archived book, clearing any reservation).

SAFETY PROPERTY: A book has archived status exactly when it appears in the archive
ledger, and an archived book never holds a reservation -- so the irreversible archival
is recorded once and leaves no dangling reservation.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od10m3p2t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Ctrls

NB == 3
TOTAL == 2
Blocks == 1..NB

VARIABLES occ, leader, alive, auth

vars == <<occ, leader, alive, auth>>

RECURSIVE SumO(_)
SumO(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
           ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN occ[x] + SumO(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ occ \in [Blocks -> 0..TOTAL]
    /\ leader \in Ctrls
    /\ alive \in SUBSET Ctrls
    /\ auth \in SUBSET Blocks

Init ==
    /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b = 1 THEN TOTAL ELSE 0]
    /\ leader = CHOOSE c \in Ctrls : TRUE
    /\ alive = Ctrls
    /\ auth = {}

GrantAuth(b) ==
    /\ leader \in alive
    /\ occ[b] >= 1
    /\ b \notin auth
    /\ auth' = auth \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, leader, alive>>

MoveFwd(b) ==
    /\ leader \in alive
    /\ b \in auth
    /\ b < NB
    /\ occ[b] >= 1
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1, ![b + 1] = @ + 1]
    /\ auth' = auth \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

MoveBack(b) ==
    /\ leader \in alive
    /\ b \in auth
    /\ b > 1
    /\ occ[b] >= 1
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1, ![b - 1] = @ + 1]
    /\ auth' = auth \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

Crash(c) ==
    /\ c \in alive
    /\ Cardinality(alive) > 1
    /\ alive' = alive \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, leader, auth>>

Elect(c) ==
    /\ leader \notin alive
    /\ c \in alive
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, alive, auth>>

Recover(c) ==
    /\ c \notin alive
    /\ alive' = alive \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, leader, auth>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : GrantAuth(b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : MoveFwd(b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : MoveBack(b)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Crash(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Elect(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Recover(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TrainConservation == SumO(Blocks) = TOTAL

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Ctrls = {c1, c2}
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TrainConservation
nl:
A subway signalling block system controls a fixed fleet of trains moving along a line
of track blocks. Trains are neither created nor destroyed; a train only moves from one
block to an adjacent block. A set of signalling controllers coordinates movement, but
only the current leader may act. Before a train can advance out of a block, the leader
must grant that block a movement authority; the train then advances forward or
backward along the line, consuming the authority. Controllers can crash silently at
any time. If the leader is among the crashed controllers, the remaining live
controllers elect a new leader (failover); a crashed controller may also later recover

CONSTANTS Agents, Doors

NONE == "none"
MAXCAP == 2

vars == <<coarse, fine, bind, sealed, cap>>

HeldFine == { d \in Doors : fine[d] # NONE }

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Agents \cup {NONE}
    /\ fine \in [Doors -> Agents \cup {NONE}]
    /\ bind \in [Doors -> Agents \cup {NONE}]
    /\ sealed \in SUBSET Doors
    /\ cap \in 1..MAXCAP

Init ==
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ fine = [d \in Doors |-> NONE]
    /\ bind = [d \in Doors |-> NONE]
    /\ sealed = {}
    /\ cap = MAXCAP

AcquireCoarse(a) ==
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ coarse' = a
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, bind, sealed, cap>>

ReleaseCoarse(a) ==
    /\ coarse = a
    /\ \A d \in Doors : fine[d] # a
    /\ coarse' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, bind, sealed, cap>>

AcquireFine(a, d) ==
    /\ coarse = a
    /\ fine[d] = NONE
    /\ Cardinality(HeldFine) < cap
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![d] = a]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, bind, sealed, cap>>

ReleaseFine(a, d) ==
    /\ fine[d] = a
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, bind, sealed, cap>>

Seal(a, d) ==
    /\ coarse = a
    /\ fine[d] = a
    /\ bind[d] = NONE
    /\ bind' = [bind EXCEPT ![d] = a]
    /\ sealed' = sealed \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, cap>>

SetCap(c) ==
    /\ c \in 1..MAXCAP
    /\ c # cap
    /\ cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, bind, sealed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Agents : AcquireCoarse(a)
    \/ \E a \in Agents : ReleaseCoarse(a)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, d \in Doors : AcquireFine(a, d)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, d \in Doors : ReleaseFine(a, d)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, d \in Doors : Seal(a, d)
    \/ \E c \in 1..MAXCAP : SetCap(c)

    \A d \in Doors :
        /\ (fine[d] # NONE) => (coarse = fine[d])
        /\ (d \in sealed) => (bind[d] # NONE)

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network uses hierarchical locking: to work on a door an agent
must first take the coarse house-wide lock, then take the fine per-door lock, and it
must release all its fine locks before releasing the coarse lock. Only one agent may
hold the coarse lock at a time, and a fine lock may be taken only by the agent that
currently holds the coarse lock. The number of fine locks that may be held at once is
a runtime capacity that can be raised or lowered on the fly. The irreversible action
is sealing a door: while holding both the coarse lock and that door's fine lock, an
agent may permanently bind the door to itself. Sealing is one-time -- once a door is
bound it can never be re-sealed or rebound.

holding no fine locks releases the coarse lock), AcquireFine (the coarse-lock holder
takes a free fine lock while below the current capacity), ReleaseFine (an agent
releases a fine lock it holds), Seal (the holder of both a door's fine lock and the
coarse lock irreversibly binds the door to itself, once), SetCap (change the fine-lock
capacity at runtime).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lock hierarchy is always respected -- any agent holding a door's
fine lock also holds the coarse lock -- and every sealed door is permanently bound to
an owner, so the irreversible seal is recorded exactly once per door.

    /\ pend' = [kind |-> "seat", p |-> p, s |-> s]

    /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![pend.p] = pend.s]

    /\ pend.kind = "seat"
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT !.kind = "none"]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, seat>>

    /\ seat[p] = NONE
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = p]
    /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![p] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pend, votes>>

    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![seat[p]] = NONE]
    /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]

    \/ \E v \in Voters : Vote(v)

    \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Slots : AdminAssign(p, s)

MutualInverse ==
    /\ \A s \in Slots : (holder[s] # NONE) => (seat[holder[s]] = s)
    /\ \A p \in Players : (seat[p] # NONE) => (holder[seat[p]] = p)

A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players into match slots. Every ordinary
seating must be approved by a quorum of the matchmaker's voting nodes: an operator
proposes seating a player into a slot, voting nodes cast approvals, and the seating is
committed only once a strict majority has approved and both the slot is empty and the
player is unseated. There are two mirrored views of the seating: the slot view records
which player holds each slot, and the player view records which slot each player sits
in; a commit updates both together. A privileged admin override can seat a player into
an empty slot immediately, bypassing the quorum, and players can leave their slot.

approves the pending seating), Commit (finalize an approved seating when slot and

cannot or should not be committed), AdminAssign (privileged immediate seating into an
empty slot for an unseated player), Leave (a seated player vacates its slot).

slot records a player then that player records that slot, and vice versa -- so no slot
is ever double-allocated to two players and no player is seated in two slots.

reconfiguration, or crash ever creates or destroys a can.

pool. Two independent matching engines, A and B, both draw from the same pool, so they
coordinate through a single compare-and-swap register that holds the number of shares
remaining in the pool. To claim a share, an engine first reads the register value, then
attempts a compare-and-swap: the claim succeeds only if the register still equals the
value it read, in which case the register is decremented and the engine credits itself
one claimed share; if the register has moved (the other engine claimed in between) the
compare-and-swap fails and the engine retries from a fresh read. Claimed shares can be
filled into matched orders, and shares can flow back to the pool either from the
claimed bucket or by unwinding a matched order. Shares are never created or destroyed.

(a successful compare-and-swap that decrements the register and credits one claimed
share), CASFail (a failed compare-and-swap whose read is now stale, cleared for retry),

claimed share to the pool, incrementing the register), UnMatch (unwind a matched order,
returning one share to the pool).

engine's claimed shares plus every engine's matched shares -- is always exactly the
fixed total, so no compare-and-swap, fill, return, or unwind ever creates or destroys

a time-limited lease. A clock advances in ticks. A lease names an owning member and an

or the current one has expired), and the owner may voluntarily drop its lease. While
holding a valid lease, a member may authorize orders; because authorization requests

executed, and once executed it can never be executed again. Executing an order that was
never authorized is forbidden.

a valid lease, and each order is executed at most once.

CONSTANTS
    Agents = {a1, a2}
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network keeps one shared configuration record (the lock
schedule) that agents update under hierarchical locking: to write, an agent must first
take the coarse house-wide lock, then the single fine record lock, so writes to the
record are fully serialized. A committed write is appended to the record's write log,
each entry recording the version the writer observed as its base. An agent may be slow
but not failed: after taking the fine lock and reading the current version, it may
delay before committing, holding the locks meanwhile; it is never treated as crashed.
On commit the log grows, the version increments, and the locks are released.

takes the free fine lock), StageRead (the fine holder reads the current version as the
base for its pending write; it may then be slow), CommitWrite (the fine holder appends
its pending write with the base it read and increments the version), ReleaseFine (the

A stock exchange opening auction maintains one shared indicative-price record that
member writers update optimistically. The record carries a version counter and the
identity of the last writer, and every committed write is recorded in an applied-writes
set stamped with the version it produced. To write, a member stages a read of the
current version, then commits only if the version it read still matches the record's
current version (an optimistic check); the commit advances the version by one and
records the applied write. If the staged read is stale (the version has moved on), the
attempt is aborted and retried, which is what prevents one member's update from
silently clobbering another's. A member may be slow but not failed: after staging a
read it may delay arbitrarily, and it may refresh its stale staged version to catch up.

reads, forcing writers to re-stage.

CommitWrite (an optimistic commit that advances the version and records the applied
write when the staged read is still current), AbortWrite (discard a staged write that
cannot commit -- stale, or when the record is already at its maximum version --
for retry), Refresh (a slow member updates its stale staged version), Reconfig (bump
the epoch and invalidate all staged reads).

writer and every applied write's version does not exceed the record's version -- so no
committed update is ever lost by being overwritten by a concurrent write at the same
version.

using optimistic locking with retry. Trains are never created or destroyed. To move a
train from a source block to a destination block, a controller first reads the current

destination and both blocks' version tags flip. If either version tag has changed
(another move touched a block) or the destination is now full, the attempt is abandoned

(change a block's capacity ceiling at runtime).

exactly the fixed fleet size -- no move, retry, or capacity re-rating ever creates or
destroys a train.

    /\ n \in alive
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, committed, alive>>

Recover(n) ==
    /\ n \notin alive
    /\ alive' = alive \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, committed, leader>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Nodes, b \in Bags, g \in Gates : Assign(l, b, g)
    \/ \E l \in Nodes, b \in Bags : Commit(l, b)
    \/ \E l \in Nodes, b \in Bags, g \in Gates : ReRoute(l, b, g)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostRouting == \A b \in Bags : (b \in committed) => (rec[b] # NONE)

nl:
An airport baggage router maintains a shared routing record mapping each bag to a gate.
A set of router nodes runs the record, with one elected leader; only a live leader may
change the record. The leader assigns a bag to a gate, and once a routing is durably
committed it is acknowledged to the airline. A committed bag may be re-routed by the
leader to a different gate (a legitimate later update), but its routing must never be
silently dropped -- that would lose an acknowledged update. Router nodes can crash; on
leader crash the live nodes elect a new leader (failover). A node may be slow but not
failed, lagging behind without being treated as crashed; crashed nodes may recover.

Actions: Assign (the live leader routes a bag to a gate), Commit (the leader durably
commits and acknowledges a bag's current routing), ReRoute (the leader changes a bag's
gate to another gate, keeping it routed), Crash (a node crashes), Elect (the live nodes
choose a new leader after the leader crashes), Recover (a crashed node rejoins).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every bag whose routing has been committed and acknowledged always has
a gate assigned in the shared record -- no acknowledged routing update is ever lost by
being dropped back to unassigned.

CONSTANTS Bays, Slots, Voters

    /\ occupied \in [Bays -> SUBSET Slots]
    /\ freeSl \in [Bays -> SUBSET Slots]
    /\ pend \in [active: BOOLEAN, bay: Bays, slot: Slots]
    /\ votes \in SUBSET Voters

Init ==
    /\ occupied = [y \in Bays |-> {}]
    /\ freeSl = [y \in Bays |-> Slots]
    /\ pend = [active |-> FALSE,
               bay |-> CHOOSE y \in Bays : TRUE,
               slot |-> CHOOSE s \in Slots : TRUE]
    /\ votes = {}

Propose(y, s) ==
    /\ ~pend.active
    /\ s \in freeSl[y]
    /\ pend' = [active |-> TRUE, bay |-> y, slot |-> s]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, freeSl>>

Vote(v) ==
    /\ pend.active
    /\ v \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, freeSl, pend>>

Place ==
    /\ pend.active
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
    /\ pend.slot \in freeSl[pend.bay]
    /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![pend.bay] = @ \cup {pend.slot}]
    /\ freeSl' = [freeSl EXCEPT ![pend.bay] = @ \ {pend.slot}]
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT !.active = FALSE]
    /\ votes' = {}

Withdraw ==
    /\ pend.active
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT !.active = FALSE]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, freeSl>>

AdminPlace(y, s) ==
    /\ s \in freeSl[y]
    /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![y] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ freeSl' = [freeSl EXCEPT ![y] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pend, votes>>

Remove(y, s) ==
    /\ s \in occupied[y]
    /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![y] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ freeSl' = [freeSl EXCEPT ![y] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pend, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E y \in Bays, s \in Slots : Propose(y, s)
    \/ \E v \in Voters : Vote(v)
    \/ Place
    \/ Withdraw
    \/ \E y \in Bays, s \in Slots : AdminPlace(y, s)
    \/ \E y \in Bays, s \in Slots : Remove(y, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

        /\ occupied[y] \cup freeSl[y] = Slots
        /\ occupied[y] \cap freeSl[y] = {}

nl:
A container-ship crane yard stacks containers into bays, where each bay has a fixed set
of stacking slots that bounds its capacity. Placing a container into a bay must be
approved by a quorum of the yard's crane controllers: an operator proposes placing a
container into a specific free slot of a bay, controllers cast approving votes, and once
a strict majority has approved the container is placed, occupying that slot. A pending
proposal may be withdrawn. A privileged yard admin can place a container into a free
slot immediately, bypassing the quorum. Containers can be removed from a slot, freeing
it.

Actions: Propose (propose placing a container into a free slot of a bay and reset the
vote tally), Vote (a controller approves the pending placement), Place (occupy the
proposed free slot once a quorum has approved), Withdraw (discard a pending placement),
AdminPlace (privileged immediate placement into a free slot), Remove (take a container
out of an occupied slot, freeing it).

SAFETY PROPERTY: In every bay the occupied slots and the free slots always partition the
bay's fixed slot set exactly -- no slot is both occupied and free and none is lost -- so
the number of containers in a bay can never exceed its slot capacity.

\* Nodes are integers 1..N so the ring successor is arithmetic.
Succ(n) == (n % N) + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ active \in SUBSET AllSlots
    /\ occupied \in SUBSET AllSlots
    /\ freeSl \in SUBSET AllSlots
    /\ holder \in Nodes

Init ==
    /\ active = AllSlots
    /\ occupied = {}
    /\ freeSl = AllSlots
    /\ holder = 1

Push(n, s) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ s \in freeSl
    /\ occupied' = occupied \cup {s}
    /\ freeSl' = freeSl \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, holder>>

Pop(s) ==
    /\ s \in occupied
    /\ occupied' = occupied \ {s}
    /\ freeSl' = freeSl \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, holder>>

PassToken(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ holder' = Succ(n)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, occupied, freeSl>>

Expand(s) ==
    /\ s \in AllSlots
    /\ s \notin active
    /\ active' = active \cup {s}
    /\ freeSl' = freeSl \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, holder>>

Shrink(s) ==
    /\ s \in freeSl
    /\ active' = active \ {s}
    /\ freeSl' = freeSl \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, holder>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, s \in AllSlots : Push(n, s)
    \/ \E s \in AllSlots : Pop(s)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : PassToken(n)
    \/ \E s \in AllSlots : Expand(s)
    \/ \E s \in AllSlots : Shrink(s)

    /\ occupied \cap freeSl = {}

nl:
An airport baggage router feeds bags into a shared sorting chute that has a variable
number of provisioned slots -- its capacity can change at runtime as slots are
commissioned or decommissioned. Exclusive access to push a bag is governed by a single
token circulating around a ring of router nodes: only the node currently holding the
token may push a bag into a free provisioned slot. Bags leave the chute when popped,
freeing their slot. Capacity is raised by provisioning a new slot (added as free) and
lowered by decommissioning a currently-free slot; an occupied slot can never be
decommissioned out from under its bag.

Actions: Push (the token holder places a bag into a free provisioned slot), Pop (a bag
leaves an occupied slot, freeing it), PassToken (the token holder hands the token to the
next node in the ring), Expand (provision a new slot, increasing capacity, added as
free), Shrink (decommission a currently-free slot, decreasing capacity).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The occupied slots and the free slots always partition exactly the set
of currently-provisioned slots -- no slot is both occupied and free, and every occupied
slot is provisioned -- so the number of bags in the chute never exceeds the current
capacity.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od9m1p6t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes

N == Cardinality(Nodes)
MAXR == 3
MAXS == 2

VARIABLES holder, round, seenRound, shedLoad

vars == <<holder, round, seenRound, shedLoad>>

\* Nodes are integers 1..N so the ring successor is arithmetic.
Succ(n) == (n % N) + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Nodes
    /\ round \in 0..MAXR
    /\ seenRound \in [Nodes -> 0..MAXR]
    /\ shedLoad \in [Nodes -> 0..MAXS]

Init ==
    /\ holder = 1
    /\ round = 1
    /\ seenRound = [n \in Nodes |-> IF n = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ shedLoad = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]

Authorized(n) == (holder = n) /\ (seenRound[n] = round)

PassToken(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ round < MAXR
    /\ holder' = Succ(n)
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ seenRound' = [seenRound EXCEPT ![Succ(n)] = round + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shedLoad>>

Shed(n) ==
    /\ Authorized(n)
    /\ shedLoad[n] < MAXS
    /\ shedLoad' = [shedLoad EXCEPT ![n] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, round, seenRound>>

Restore(n) ==
    /\ Authorized(n)
    /\ shedLoad[n] > 0
    /\ shedLoad' = [shedLoad EXCEPT ![n] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, round, seenRound>>

Balance(n, m) ==
    /\ Authorized(n)
    /\ n # m
    /\ shedLoad[n] > 0
    /\ shedLoad[m] < MAXS
    /\ shedLoad' = [shedLoad EXCEPT ![n] = @ - 1, ![m] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, round, seenRound>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : PassToken(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Shed(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Restore(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, m \in Nodes : Balance(n, m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CurrentTokenUnique ==
    { n \in Nodes : seenRound[n] = round } = {holder}

nl:
A power-grid load shedder is run by a ring of substation nodes that pass a single
authority token around the ring. Each time the token is handed on, the token round
number advances and the receiving node records the new round as the round it has seen.
Only the node that currently holds the token and whose seen-round matches the current
round is authorized to shed load; a node that once held the token but has since passed
it on is a stale participant and must not act, even though it is still live (slow but
not failed). Authorized shedding lets the holder shed a load unit at its own bus,
restore a shed unit, or rebalance one shed unit to another node.

Actions: PassToken (the holder hands the token to the next node in the ring, advancing
the round and stamping the new holder's seen-round), Shed (the authorized holder sheds
one load unit at its bus), Restore (the authorized holder restores one shed unit),
Balance (the authorized holder moves one shed unit from its bus to another node).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every node other than the current token holder has a strictly stale
seen-round (behind the current round), so only the current holder ever carries a
current-round token and no unauthorized or stale participant can act.
